title: Recombinant Zoster Vaccine (Shingrix) Adult Schedule
keywords: shingrix zoster shingles vaccine rzv 2-dose series zostavax immunization
text: CDC ACIP recommends a 2-dose series of recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix, CVX 187) 2 to 6 months apart for adults aged >=50 years (and >=19 years if immunodeficient or immunosuppressed), regardless of prior herpes zoster or prior live zoster vaccine (Zostavax, CVX 121). A single administered RZV dose completes only 1 of 2 required doses.

title: Seasonal COVID-19 and Influenza Vaccination Cadence
keywords: covid-19 sars-cov-2 influenza flu seasonal vaccine booster up to date
text: CDC ACIP recommends updated seasonal COVID-19 vaccination and annual seasonal influenza vaccination. COVID-19 or influenza doses administered more than 12 months prior to the current clinical anchor date reflect historical seasons rather than current-season protection.

title: Adult Tdap and Decennial Td/Tdap Booster Schedule
keywords: tdap td tetanus diphtheria pertussis booster pregnancy 10 years vaccine
text: CDC ACIP recommends 1 dose of Tdap for adults who have not previously received Tdap (and 1 Tdap dose during every pregnancy at 27-36 weeks gestation), followed by a Td or Tdap booster every 10 years.

title: Adult Pneumococcal and RSV Vaccination Guidance
keywords: pneumococcal pcv20 pcv21 ppsv23 prevnar rsv respiratory syncytial virus vaccine
text: CDC ACIP recommends pneumococcal conjugate vaccination (PCV20 or PCV21, or PCV15 followed by PPSV23) for adults aged >=50 years and adults 19-49 years with chronic heart, lung, liver, renal, or diabetes risk conditions, and a single RSV vaccine dose for adults >=75 years or 60-74 years at increased risk.

title: HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitor (Statin) Class Duplication Safety
keywords: statin atorvastatin lipitor simvastatin zocor rosuvastatin crestor pravastatin duplicate cholesterol myopathy rhabdomyolysis
text: Atorvastatin (Lipitor), simvastatin (Zocor), rosuvastatin (Crestor), and pravastatin (Pravachol) belong to the same HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin) class (WHO-ATC C10AA). Concurrent use of two statins represents therapeutic class duplication that increases dose-dependent risk of myopathy, elevated creatine kinase, and rhabdomyolysis without additive cardiovascular benefit; prescribers reconcile to a single statin.

title: Concurrent Benzodiazepine, Z-Drug Hypnotic, and Opioid CNS Depression
keywords: lorazepam ativan diazepam valium alprazolam xanax zolpidem ambien trazodone oxycodone sedative hypnotic sleep falls sedation
text: Combining benzodiazepines (such as lorazepam/Ativan, diazepam/Valium, alprazolam/Xanax) with non-benzodiazepine Z-drug sedative-hypnotics (such as zolpidem/Ambien) or opioids produces additive central nervous system depression, daytime psychomotor impairment, confusion, falls, and respiratory depression, particularly in older adults. Sudden benzodiazepine discontinuation can precipitate withdrawal; medication changes require clinician supervision.

title: Anticoagulant, Antiplatelet, and NSAID Concurrent Bleeding Risk
keywords: warfarin coumadin apixaban eliquis rivaroxaban xarelto clopidogrel plavix aspirin ibuprofen naproxen meloxicam nsaid bleeding thinner
text: Oral anticoagulants (warfarin, apixaban/Eliquis, rivaroxaban/Xarelto) and antiplatelet agents (clopidogrel/Plavix, aspirin) increase gastrointestinal and systemic hemorrhage risk when co-administered with systemic NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen, meloxicam) or dual antithrombotic regimens. Patients should report melena, hematuria, or unexplained bruising and review pain alternatives with their clinician before altering antithrombotic therapy.

title: NSAID Nephrotoxicity and Hemodynamic Kidney Injury in CKD / Heart Failure
source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD Evaluation and Management
keywords: nsaid ibuprofen naproxen meloxicam creatinine egfr kidney ckd lisinopril losartan furosemide acute kidney injury
text: Systemic NSAIDs inhibit prostaglandin-mediated afferent arteriolar vasodilation, reducing glomerular filtration, promoting sodium/fluid retention, and precipitating acute kidney injury - especially in Chronic Kidney Disease (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2) or alongside ACE inhibitors/ARBs/ARNIs and loop or thiazide diuretics.

title: HbA1c Reference Range, Abnormally Low HbA1c (<4.0%), and Hypoglycemia Assessment
source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes
keywords: hba1c a1c hemoglobin glucose hypoglycemia insulin glipizide sulfonylurea low normal reference range diabetes
text: Standard non-diabetic adult HbA1c is 4.0-5.6% (>=6.5% diagnostic of diabetes; <7.0% common glycemic target for many non-pregnant adults). An HbA1c <4.0% is below the physiologic reference interval and warrants evaluation for frequent/unrecognized hypoglycemia (particularly in patients treated with insulin or sulfonylureas), hemolysis/shortened erythrocyte lifespan, hemoglobin variants, or recent transfusion.

title: Metformin and SGLT2 Inhibitor Renal Function (eGFR) Thresholds
keywords: metformin glucophage empagliflozin jardiance dapagliflozin farxiga egfr creatinine kidney lactic acidosis
text: FDA labeling contraindicates metformin when eGFR is <30 mL/min/1.73m2 due to lactic acidosis risk and advises reassessing benefit/risk and avoiding starting metformin when eGFR is 30-44 mL/min/1.73m2. SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin) provide cardiorenal protection down to guideline-specified eGFR initiation thresholds.

title: KDIGO Chronic Kidney Disease GFR Categories and Monitoring
keywords: ckd chronic kidney disease egfr stage g3a g3b g4 g5 creatinine albuminuria
text: KDIGO stages CKD by persistent GFR: G1 (>=90), G2 (60-89), G3a (45-59, mild-to-moderate decrease), G3b (30-44, moderate-to-severe), G4 (15-29, severe), and G5 (<15 mL/min/1.73m2, kidney failure), paired with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (A1 <30, A2 30-300, A3 >300 mg/g).

title: Heart Failure GDMT and Hyperkalemia Monitoring (RAASi/ARNI + MRA + Potassium)
keywords: heart failure entresto sacubitril valsartan lisinopril spironolactone aldactone potassium hyperkalemia furosemide
text: Combining RAAS blockers (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or sacubitril/valsartan) with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (spironolactone, eplerenone) or oral potassium chloride supplements raises hyperkalemia risk (serum potassium >5.1 mmol/L), requiring serial electrolyte and renal function monitoring. ACE inhibitors and sacubitril/valsartan must never be taken concurrently (36-hour washout required).

title: Warfarin INR Therapeutic Range and Supratherapeutic Monitoring
keywords: warfarin coumadin inr prothrombin anticoagulation vitamin k bleeding target
text: In non-anticoagulated adults, normal INR is 0.8-1.2; for most warfarin indications (atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism), the standard therapeutic INR target is 2.0-3.0 (2.5-3.5 for certain mechanical heart valves). INR values >3.5-4.0 elevate major bleeding risk and require prompt clinician review of interacting medications, acute illness, and dietary vitamin K changes.

title: PD-1/PD-L1 Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Immune-Related Adverse Events (irAEs)
source: NCI / ASCO Immune-Related Adverse Event Management Guideline
keywords: pembrolizumab keytruda nivolumab opdivo immunotherapy checkpoint thyroiditis tsh pneumonitis colitis hepatitis
text: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors (such as pembrolizumab/Keytruda and nivolumab/Opdivo) can cause delayed immune-related adverse events across organ systems, including immune-mediated thyroid dysfunction (hyperthyroid phase followed by hypothyroidism on TSH/free T4), pneumonitis (new cough/dyspnea/hypoxia), hepatitis (elevated ALT/AST/bilirubin), and colitis, requiring serial organ-panel monitoring.

title: Prenatal Anemia, Thyroid, and Glycemic Monitoring in Pregnancy
keywords: pregnancy prenatal gestational diabetes iron anemia hemoglobin tsh levothyroxine tdap maternal
text: Routine prenatal care includes screening for iron-deficiency anemia (hemoglobin <11.0 g/dL in 1st/3rd trimesters or <10.5 g/dL in 2nd trimester), gestational diabetes screening (typically 24-28 weeks, or earlier with risk factors), TSH monitoring when receiving levothyroxine (separate oral iron/calcium from levothyroxine by >=4 hours to prevent malabsorption), and Tdap vaccination at 27-36 weeks.

title: Multi-Organization Medication Reconciliation Across Care Transitions
source: AHRQ Care Transitions & Medication Reconciliation Guide
keywords: reconciliation discharge outpatient pharmacy brand generic discrepancy duplicate care transition
text: When health records combine multiple care organizations or hospital discharge summaries, brand-generic naming differences (for example Lipitor vs atorvastatin, Plavix vs clopidogrel, Eliquis vs apixaban, Aldactone vs spironolactone, Ativan vs lorazepam, Ambien vs zolpidem) and unclosed prior orders frequently create apparent duplicates or discrepancies that should be confirmed with the prescribing care team.
